title: How to Make Herb‑Infused Butter Balls for Easter Brunch
meta_description: Learn how to make herb‑infused butter balls for Easter brunch with easy steps, using Herb Scissors for perfectly minced herbs every time.
html:
When the spring sun starts to warm the kitchen, nothing says celebration like herb‑infused butter balls for Easter brunch. The secret to a bright, evenly‑distributed herb flavor is using a tool that can mince cilantro, chives, and basil in a single snip—enter the Herb Scissors. In this guide we’ll walk through the butter‑ball technique, from selecting fresh herbs to shaping the perfect bite‑size spheres, so you can serve a buttery, aromatic spread that impresses both family and guests.

Gathering Your Ingredients and Tools

Start with high‑quality butter. Unsalted, cultured butter offers a creamy tang that pairs beautifully with fresh herbs. You’ll need:

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 tablespoons fresh chives, finely minced
  • 1 tablespoon fresh basil, finely minced
  • 1 teaspoon fresh cilantro, finely minced
  • 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest (optional)
  • Sea salt and cracked black pepper to taste

For tools, besides a mixing bowl and rubber spatula, the Herb Scissors are essential. Their five‑blade design lets you snip herbs quickly and uniformly, while the built‑in cleaning comb makes cleanup a breeze.

Using Herb Scissors for Perfectly Minced Herbs

Place the herb stems into the scissors and close the blades. One snip yields a fine, even chop—no need to waste time with a cutting board and knife. The result is a bright, fragrant herb mixture that integrates seamlessly into the butter. If you’re new to the Herb Scissors, give them a quick rinse with the cleaning comb after each use; the comb removes any lingering bits of leaf and keeps the blades sharp.

Mixing the Butter and Herbs

In a large bowl, add the softened butter. Using a rubber spatula, create a well in the center and dump the minced chives, basil, and cilantro. Sprinkle in the lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Fold the herbs into the butter until the mixture is uniform, but be careful not to over‑mix; you want the herbs to stay distinct for texture and visual appeal.

Tip: If the butter feels too soft, chill it for 5‑10 minutes before shaping. This makes the butter easier to handle and helps the herbs stay suspended rather than sinking to the bottom.

Forming and Freezing Butter Balls

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Scoop out about one tablespoon of the herb butter and roll it between your palms to form a smooth ball. Place each ball on the sheet and repeat until the mixture is used up. For consistent size, use a small ice‑cream scoop or a teaspoon as a guide.

Once all the balls are on the sheet, freeze them for at least 30 minutes. The chill locks in the herb flavor and gives the butter a firm, bite‑size shape that won’t melt when served alongside warm dishes.

Serving Ideas for Easter Brunch

Herb‑infused butter balls are versatile. Here are a few ways to incorporate them into your Easter spread:

  • Warm rolls and croissants: Place a butter ball on a fresh roll just before serving; the heat will melt it into a glossy glaze.
  • Roasted vegetables: Toss carrots, asparagus, or new potatoes with a butter ball that melts over the top for a glossy, herb‑kissed finish.
  • Egg dishes: Add a butter ball to scrambled eggs or a frittata right before plating for a burst of flavor.

Because the balls are pre‑portioned, guests can add as much or as little butter as they like, keeping the brunch tidy and elegant.

Storing Leftover Butter Balls

If you make more than you need, the butter balls keep well. Transfer the frozen balls to an airtight container or a zip‑top bag, then store them in the freezer for up to three months. When you’re ready to use them, simply unwrap a ball and let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes; it will soften enough to spread or melt without losing shape.

FAQ

Can I use dried herbs instead of fresh?

Dried herbs lack the bright flavor and moisture of fresh herbs, so the butter won’t have the same pop. If you must use dried, reduce the quantity to one‑third and add a pinch of extra salt to compensate.

What if I don’t have Herb Scissors?

You can still achieve good results with a sharp chef’s knife, but the herbs may be unevenly chopped, leading to pockets of flavor rather than a consistent taste throughout the butter.

Are these butter balls gluten‑free?

Yes. The butter balls contain only butter, herbs, and seasonings, making them safe for gluten‑free diets as long as you serve them with gluten‑free accompaniments.
